This page is for SCGSim contributors. It describes how runs and results are
identified. Users only need [Read returned results](course/returned-results.qmd).

## What identifies a run

A run or report binds, as applicable:

- SCGSim distribution version and measured runtime-source module/content identity;
- SCGSim Git revision observation when available, and backend revision;
- Geometry source, compiler and topology identity;
- solver and schema version;
- machine profile and run receipt;
- config, mesh, handoff, result, and report artifact identities;
- validation and failure state.

Use the returned package together with its preparation-side source and model
notes. A distribution version alone does not identify the runtime code bytes,
layout, settings or native result of a particular study. The current
runtime-source manifest and content digest identify the module bytes used for
execution; a Git revision is recorded only when truthfully available.

The current Palace geometry authority is `scgsim.geometry.compiler`. Palace
continues to serialize the established `scgsim_sgb` field, whose current value
names that authority. The field name does not request an import from the former
package. Historical receipt values and runtime-source inventories retain the
module identities they recorded and are not rewritten to the current paths.

## AEDT receipt cohorts {#aedt-receipt-cohorts}

New handoffs retain `scgsim.aedt.handoff.v1` and
`scgsim.aedt.handoff-manifest.v1`. Both records add
`expected_receipt_schema: scgsim.aedt.receipt.v3`, and the initial receipt is
V3. It contains `prepared_runtime_source`: a deterministic, sorted
`runtime-source.v19` manifest. The record fields are
`schema_version`, `stage`, `modules`, `content_sha256`, and
`revision_observation`; there is no helper-hash map. Each declared module has
measured bytes and the content digest binds that inventory. The Git observation
is either available with the actual 40-hex commit or explicitly unavailable.
A source checkout or fabricated revision is not required for byte-bound
identity.

Before writing `running`, the shared transaction accepts its established
initial-receipt cohorts: a V3 receipt with both V3 expectation markers and a
canonical manifest; a V2 receipt with both V2 markers and a canonical
manifest; or an exact V1 `not_run` receipt with both markers absent and the
canonical historical manifest. A historical handoff may continue through its
supported family path under those cohort rules; this does not bypass family
request requirements.

Every new Q3D or HFSS 3D execution requires explicit `modeling`; a
`thin_film` request also needs its corresponding source declarations before
receipt mutation. A previously supported Q3D/HFSS result payload without
`modeling` remains under its original reader and hash interpretation and cannot
start a new execution. The shared V1/V2 handoff compatibility remains
available to unchanged families such as Q2D, but does not bypass the current
Q3D/HFSS request requirement. Q3D input-v1 and input-v2 request schemas remain
removed.

The verified initial-receipt hash and prepared-manifest hash are copied into
the mutable V3 receipt. The final receipt is intentionally not compared with
its initial hash because execution must mutate it. Unknown versions, mixed or
partial markers, noncanonical members, and hash mismatches reject before
receipt mutation.

Every new completed V3 receipt has a separate `runtime_source` manifest using
`runtime-source.v19` and a content digest for the code that actually executed
it. Declared module bytes and the digest are mandatory; V19 has no redundant
helper-hash fields. `revision_observation` carries the actual 40-hex commit
when available and records `unavailable` truthfully for an immutable wheel
without VCS metadata. Missing or corrupt declared module bytes, digest, schema,
or cohort still fails closed. Preparation and execution hashes are evidence
with different timing, not an equality requirement, and historical hashes are
not compared to the currently installed package.

`resolve_results()` preserves the existing rules for genuine historical
completed V1 and V2 receipts. A receipt relabeled below its preparation markers
is an inconsistent downgrade and rejects. V2 and V3 resolution verify their
exact cohorts, markers, canonical prepared manifest, initial-receipt binding,
and complete actual runtime manifest before applying their version-specific
family result checks. Only V3 HFSS completion requires sealed native PEC binding
evidence; this requirement is never projected onto historical V1/V2 receipts.
These unsigned consistency checks do not authenticate an artifact set against
an actor able to rewrite every member.

`runtime-source.v1` is a frozen thirteen-module reader contract, not a live
enumeration rule. The V2–V14 inventories are frozen as well. V4 added
`scgsim/aedt/_presentation.py`; V5 added `scgsim/sgb/geometry_plan.py` and
`scgsim/sgb/__init__.py`. V7 added
`scgsim/_notebook_presentation.py` to V6. V8 added
`scgsim/aedt/_junction_partition.py` to V7. V9 added
`scgsim/aedt/__init__.py`, `scgsim/aedt/_q3d_geometry.py`,
`scgsim/sgb/adapter.py`, and `scgsim/sgb/stack.py` to V8. V10 added the shared
`scgsim/aedt/_handoff_cohort.py` to V9; V11 added
`scgsim/aedt/_q3d_bodies.py` to V10. V12 is frozen with V11's exact path
membership. V13 retains its frozen inventory, mandatory declared module bytes
and digest, and optional `revision_observation`; V1–V17 retain their frozen path
membership, field meanings, and version-specific reader rules. V16 added the HFSS Eigenmode native implementation module to the
V15 inventory. V17 added the shared lumped-model and HFSS lumped-native modules,
plus the AEDT specs package initializer, to V16. V18 removed the former
EPR-private `epr/junction_partition.py` path and included
`preparation/junction_partition.py`, the relocated AEDT data/RLC/terminal
helpers, geometry/EPR/support specs, modeling/planar preparation, HFSS geometry
runtime, neutral geometry representation modules, and the shared source-ground
construction helper with its polygon-operation leaf. The current V19 inventory
adds the model-only prepared-model reader. V19 uses the same five record fields
described above and no helper-hash map; its exact path list is the declared
implementation inventory. These manifests bind their
declared file inventories, not an exhaustive transitive dependency
attestation. The frozen V12 inventory, for example, does not separately hash
`scgsim/sgb/engine_gates.py`. They do not change the V3 receipt schema. A pure
initial-receipt codec owns exact V1/V2/V3 member
order, two-space JSON indentation, and the trailing newline. V1 omits prepared
provenance; V2 and V3 insert it between `source` and `outputs`. Reading
historical evidence uses the declared frozen schema and does not compare
historical hashes with the installed package.

Execution computes mandatory runtime-source provenance inside the receipt-bound
failure transaction, before importing PyAEDT or constructing Desktop. Current
V19 may record `revision_observation` as unavailable; that alone does not fail
byte-bound identity or prevent execution. Missing or corrupt declared module
bytes, digest, schema, or cohort still yield a failed V3 receipt without a
Desktop launch rather than escaping receipt finalization. V1–V17 retain their
version-specific historical validation rules, including revision requirements
where declared.

The family save contract remains fail-closed. `save_project()` returning false
before solve aborts before native execution; returning false after export aborts
before completion is reported. SCGSim does not turn either state into a new
partial-success receipt or infer that native project bytes are usable.

## Native run coverage {#native-run-coverage}

Which workflows have been run end to end (prepare, native solve, resolve,
report), and with which build:

The baseline facade exports and documented direct submodule surfaces for
geometry/compiler, AEDT, Palace and visualization are mapped in the
[API migration](api-migration.qmd) page. Six earlier full native-to-Resolve-to-Report observations
are bound to the earlier wheel with SHA256
`48963671d4f854c185b8f95f3cd8000960355a7c48550b9ccf19b739b49f8df3` and
runtime-source v13 content digest
`42b48f3d5946fadb1e93e92a1d3eb2a55f72ff00fc41aeccf71c0fded5919fa1`; those
observations cover CPW Modal and Terminal, Q2D, Q3D AC/RL, SimplePad Q3D C/G,
and Palace ES, and are not current-wheel execution evidence. Separately, the
frozen `2.0.0.dev1` candidate wheel with SHA256
`e0ab1117aad4e5578ec98251732d33f6faa2fe7524dd70dcbc44891ed024824d` had a
Q3D build-only/readback/save/release observation and geometry preview, without
`Analyze`, solve, or C/G matrices.

The full Xmon Palace Eigenmode Route A, CircularPad Palace Eigenmode Route B,
and HFSS Eigenmode saved-field EPR/offline-loss operations were not observed as
complete native-to-Resolve-to-Report workflows. Q3D input-v1/v2 readers remain absent.

## Publication boundary

Public SCGSim documentation and fixtures must contain no private names, paths,
dimensions, screenshots, meshes, configs, receipts, data, or artifacts.
Sanitization alone does not grant publication authority.

Private consumer validation may inform a public aggregate statement only when
the statement has separate publication authority and contains no private
identity or payload.
